title: Adaptive spec-deploy gatekeeper and KV watermark draft
summary: Draft design for an adaptive deployment gatekeeper for speculative decoding that coordinates kernel admission, KV cache watermarks, and rate-aware admission to enable safe rollouts and fast rollback. Includes acceptance criteria, telemetry design, and operational runbook.
content:
Purpose and scope

This doc proposes an operational and technical pattern for onboarding speculative decoding changes (kernels, scheduler heuristics, and KV cache behaviour) into the serving runtime with automated gatekeeping and clear rollback contracts. The goal is to let us safely enable speculative kernels and scheduler policies in production without creating cascading latency or correctness regressions.

We call the pattern the Adaptive Spec-Deploy Gatekeeper (ASDG). ASDG is a lightweight admission layer that sits in the request path and in the model admission pipeline to decide, per-request and per-model, whether to:
- permit speculative decode flows (fast-path kernels + early-emission hooks)
- allow KV-prefix caching/admission for speculative state
- fall back to conservative (non-speculative) kernels when risk signals exceed thresholds

Design principles
- Incremental: changes should be incrementally enabled per-model and per-route, not globally.
- Observable: every admission decision must be annotated with structured telemetry for offline analysis.
- Revertible: automated and manual rollback must be simple and fast with clear abort criteria.
- Workload-aware: decisions must consider request size, token-rate, latency percentiles, and backend GPU load.
- Quality-aware: output quality regressions must be continuously measured against a small canary eval set and flagged.

Core components
1) Admission controller (lightweight runtime module)
- Inputs: model id/version, customer tier, route config, request metadata (batch size, max tokens, user-priority), current node load snapshot, policy flags (canary percent, features).
- Outputs: admission decision (speculative-enabled | conservative), admission-reason code, token_budget_reservation_id (for accounting).
- Implementation notes: controller should be async-fast path; decision latency <= 200us median. Cache decisions for identical request fingerprints for 5s to reduce CPU overhead.

2) KV watermark controller
- Purpose: track how much speculative state is allowed to be cached per-node and per-model. Prevent KV cache thrash from speculative prefixes.
- Watermarks: low, soft, hard. Each watermark maps to eviction aggressiveness and admission probability.
- Behaviour: when node KV usage < low watermark -> speculative admission allowed. Between low and soft -> admission probabilistic (e.g., linear decay). Above hard watermark -> block speculative writes; allow reads only.
- Eviction policy: prioritize reclaiming speculative segments (marked with speculative flag) before stable segments. Record evictions in telemetry.

3) Kernel handshake protocol
- On admission, runtime flags the token stream with kernel_hint="speculative-vX". Kernels that accept that hint must implement the following handshake: negotiate kv-consistency-level (strict|best-effort), provide rewind window size (tokens), and emit a readiness token. If handshake fails, runtime falls back before token emission.

4) Rate-aware admission and throttles
- Admission should consider global throughput and per-model reserved capacity. If an incoming burst would exceed the reserved burst capacity, admission must probabilistically deny speculative mode to maintain SLOs.
- For hosted customers with token quotas, we also include cost-accounting: speculative admission requires reserving a small extra token budget to account for rewinds/retries.

Acceptance criteria for onboarding
We will only consider a model variant (kernel/scheduler change) accepted for gradual rollout if it meets the following in controlled canaries:
- Latency: p95 tail latency for user-visible tokens must remain within +10% of baseline and p99 within +20% across a representative synthetic workload.
- Throughput: aggregate tokens/sec should be >= baseline under identical concurrency.
- Cost per token: measured GPU cycles per emitted token must not exceed baseline by more than 15% (accounting for rewinds).
- Rewind rate: percentage of requests that required a rewind must be < 1% for steady-state production traffic mix.
- KV hit-rate impact: stable prefix hit-rate degradation <= 2% (speculative prefixes should not starve stable cache).
- Quality: auto-eval score on the canary prompt set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity depending on task) must not drop by more than 1.5 points absolute or 3% relative.
- Error rate: model-returned errors (exceptions, OOMs, kernel panics) must be <= baseline + 0.25%.

If any of the above fail during the canary run, the variant is rejected and operator should run the rollback procedure.

Rollback contract and automated safety nets
- Automated abort: ASDG watches a small set of SLI windows (latency p99, error rate, KV eviction spikes, CPU/GPU utilization). If any SLI crosses the abort threshold (defined as baseline * multiplier) for sustained 30s, ASDG flips the model variant to conservative for all traffic and emits an urgent alert.
- Quick rollback CLI: a single command (rci rollback-model --model model:ver) should mark the variant as disabled in the gatekeeper and initiate a distributed flush so future requests avoid speculative writes.
- KV cleanup: post-rollback, speculative KV segments are cleaned incrementally to avoid a large eviction load. Cleaning is rate-limited and prioritized by creation timestamp.
- Safety snapshot: when first enabling a variant in canary, take a snapshot of KV usage and kernel metrics to allow post-mortem comparisons.

Telemetry and metrics (proposal)
All telemetry should be tagged with model_id, model_version, node_id, route, admission_mode, and the kernel_hint. Metric names are prefixed with runtime.speculative. Below are proposed metrics (Prometheus-friendly names):
- runtime.speculative.admissions_total (labels: decision, reason)
- runtime.speculative.admission_latency_ms_bucket (histogram)
- runtime.speculative.rewinds_total (labels: reason)
- runtime.speculative.rewind_latency_ms_histogram
- runtime.speculative.kv_evictions_speculative_total
- runtime.speculative.kv_evictions_stable_total
- runtime.speculative.kv_usage_bytes (gauge per node)
- runtime.speculative.kv_speculative_ratio (gauge: speculative_bytes / total_kv_bytes)
- runtime.speculative.kv_watermark_state (0=low,1=soft,2=hard)
- runtime.speculative.kernel_handshake_failures_total
- runtime.speculative.quality.eval_score_change (task-tagged gauge sampled periodically)
- runtime.speculative.per_token_gpu_cycles (summary)
Telemetry events / structured logs (samples):
- {ts, model, ver, node, request_id, admission:allowed, admission_reason: 'kv_low', kernel_hint: 'spec-v3', rewind_window: 8, kv_alloc_made: 1024}

Operational playbook (short)
Enable variant in dev/staging: run the test harness with the canary prompt suite and injection of noisy background load. Validate metrics offline.
Enable 1% production canary: monitor the telemetry panel with explicit alert thresholds (latency_p99 > baseline*1.2 or error_rate > baseline + 0.25%).
If alerts fire:
1) ASDG should automatically flip admissions to conservative; page on-call and post a status in #serving-runtime.
2) Run quick rollback CLI to block variant and initiate KV cleanup.
3) Collect artifacts: acceptance snapshot, node traces, kernel logs, and a sample of user requests (with PII redaction).
4) Post-mortem with 48-hour SLA for initial diagnosis.

Quality monitoring and eval integration
- Continuous micro-evals: run a small representative prompt set on a sample of production traffic via a shadowing harness. Compute embedding similarity and a lightweight hallucination detector. If quality drift is detected (score delta > configured threshold) block further canary ramp.
- Human-in-the-loop: for selected customer-facing routes, route a 0.5% percentage of responses to a human review queue during initial ramps for subjective quality checks.

Test harness and acceptance automation
We will extend the existing speculative decode test harness (linked) to support:
- workload replay with realistic concurrency and token distributions (short/long mixes)
- KV-pressure injection (simulate many speculative prefixes with varying TTLs)
- kernel handshake failure injection (simulate handshake timeout to validate fast fallback)
- smoke benchmarks that assert p95/p99 targets and record per-token GPU cycle estimates

Implementation notes and developer guidance
- Prefer conservative defaults: the gatekeeper default should deny speculative admission unless a model explicitly opts in.
- Short-circuiting: controllers should add decision info to the request trace to simplify debugging (trace span: "spec-decision").
- Deterministic seeds: probabilistic admission (when using soft watermarks) should use a deterministic hash of request_id and window to keep ramp behaviour reproducible in experiments.
- Lightweight feature flags: model teams should be able to set variant flags (spec-vX) and per-route percentages via the Console; those flags feed ASDG.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Where should rewind accounting live? We currently track rewinds on the serving node that initiated the speculative emission; this requires cross-node correlation when handoffs happen. Tradeoff: central accounting is simpler to reason about but adds latency to the admission path.
- How quickly to decay speculative cache entries after rollback? Aggressive cleanup reduces memory pressure but creates eviction storms. We propose a rate-limited decay with backoff.
- Acceptance thresholds are conservative; we will tighten once we have more coverage.

Appendix: example alert thresholds (initial)
- p99 latency increase > 1.2x baseline sustained 30s -> automated conservative flip + page oncall
- error rate > baseline + 0.25% sustained 30s -> automated conservative flip + page
- kv_speculative_ratio > 0.35 -> reduce admission probability to 10%
- rewind_rate > 1% over 5m -> reduce admission probability, evaluate kernel regressions

Appendix: quick rollback steps (operator)
1) rci rollback-model --model modelname:ver
2) Check ASDG decisions: rci show-admissions --model modelname:ver --last 5m
3) Trigger KV cleanup: rci kv-cleanup --model modelname:ver --mode gradual
4) Verify stable KV hit-rate returns to baseline and monitor spec metrics for 15m.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative and verbose to avoid blind spots during rollout. Please focus review on: the KV watermark parameters, the handshake contract (rewind window semantics), and the automated abort thresholds.
- If you have a counterproposal for acceptance thresholds please add it inline or in the linked GH PR.

-- end of draft
